# Near

I used 1024-bit primes for RSA encryption, so there's no way you can recover my message, right?

Here's the code I used:
```python
from Crypto.Util.number import bytes_to_long, getPrime
from sympy import nextprime
from pathlib import Path

flag = Path("flag.txt").read_bytes()
m = bytes_to_long(flag)
p = getPrime(1024)
q = nextprime(p)
n = p * q
e = 65537
c = pow(m, e, n)
print(f"n = {n}")
print(f"e = {e}")
print(f"c = {c}")
```

## Solution

In order to attempt to exploit flaws in RSA values given, we can use a tool called RsaCtfTool: <https://github.com/RsaCtfTool/RsaCtfTool>

This tool will try several mathematical attacks on RSA to see if there is an easy way to exploit an RSA implementation. The command ran is below:

`./RsaCtfTool.py -n  -e 65537 --uncipher `

The Python script tells us the attack was successful with the fermat method, and prints the result of decrypting the ciphertext.
